ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Post-Training Quantization of VGGT for Multi-View 3D Reconstruction
PROPOSAL: Experimentally estimate the impact of post-training quantization methods (such as linear and logarithmic quantization) on the accuracy of VGGT for multi-view 3D reconstruction tasks, including camera pose estimation, point map, and point cloud reconstruction.
CONTROLS: Compare against a baseline of full-precision VGGT and ablate the roles of the camera and register tokens in the quantization process.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect to see accuracy drops in camera pose estimation and point map regression due to the heavy-tailed activation distributions of the data-independent special tokens, but potential gains in point cloud reconstruction due to the reduction of floating point precision errors. The extent of these losses and potential gains will depend on the specific post-training quantization method used.

Assumptions:
- VGGT is fine-tuned on a sub-sampling of its original training set to save compute.
- The calibration set consists of a small batch of real-world multi-view images.
- The experiments are performed on standard synthetic and real-world benchmarks for multi-view 3D reconstruction.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Constrained Minimization for Quantizing VGGT's Activation Statistics
PROPOSAL: Develop a regularized optimization framework that seeks to minimize the difference in quantization error between the pre- and post-quantization activations of the special tokens, while constraining the quantization ranges to satisfy a set of empirically-derived or theoretically-derived constraints (e.g., bounds on tail blows-up and increase in entropy). This approach is expected to handle heavy-tailed distributions more effectively than standard quantization methods.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed constrained minimization framework to standard quantization methods and a baseline of full-precision VGGT on a set of commonly used 3D reconstruction benchmarks. We will also analyze the impact of different regularization terms (e.g., L1/L2-norm penalty) on the results.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate significant improvements in accuracy due to more effective handling of heavy-tailed activation distributions, especially when applied to the camera and register tokens. Potential failures could arise from difficulties in imposing the constraints in practice, or from competing accomplishments of different regularizations, especially in highly-complex scenes.

Assumptions:
- The regularization constraints can be effectively derived from the data and activation statistics of VGGT.
- The computational overhead of the optimization problem remains reasonable given the available hardware.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: Constrained Minimization for Quantizing VGGT's Activation Statistics
PROPOSAL: Refine the constrained minimization framework to incorporate explicit uncertainty bounding and surrogate modeling, allowing the estimation of the distribution of the quantization error under plausible distributions of the input data. This enables the formulation of tighter constraints and leading to satisfying more of the prespecified requirements, while also enabling insights into the performance uncertainty of VGGT under real-world scenarios. The method will be constructed by application of recent probabilistic deep learning calibration techniques (e.g., calibration via entropy regularization).
CONTROLS: Compare this generalized version of constrained minimization against the original version on both standard benchmarks and on real-world datasets (e.g, FlyingThings3D). Additionally, compare the results against the state-of-the-art quantization methods specifically designed for transformers.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We anticipate significant improvements in accuracy and more reliable uncertainty estimates. However, failures in high-entropy scenarios might occur, and defining suitable regularizers will be challenging.

Assumptions:
- Effective surrogates for the uncertain quantization can be found during training.
- Calibration remains feasible with significant reduction in accuracy.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Exponential Moving Averages for Sampling Calibrating Data
PROPOSAL: Refine the Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs) sampling method for calibrating data by incorporating a key observation from the Analysis of Activation Statistics (Proposal 4) that calibration sampling method can significantly affect the activation statistics, especially in the presence of data-independent special tokens. Introduce a bias correction term in the EMA update rule to mitigate potential biases in the sampling process.
CONTROLS: Compare the revised EMA method against the baseline random sampling method, and against an ablated version of the EMA method without the bias correction term. Investigate the robustness of the revised EMA method on different VGGT setups and datasets.
COST: 800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The revised EMA method is expected to provide a better trade-off between calibration accuracy and computational efficiency, reducing the potential for bias in calibration sampling. However, its performance may degrade in scenarios with extreme outliers or limited calibration data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-agnostic Variance Control for Post-Training Quantization
PROPOSAL: Develop a variance control mechanism for post-training quantization that can be applied to any quantization method, including those that are not variance-controlled, such as linear quantization. This mechanism uses techniques from variance-based risk analysis and uncertainty quantification to control the variance of the quantized model, ensuring that the resulting model has a desired level of accuracy and robustness.
CONTROLS: Compare the proposed model-agnostic variance control mechanism against existing variance-controlled quantization methods (e.g., calibrated quantization, split-learning). Investigate its application to different VGGT setups and datasets.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The proposed model-agnostic variance control mechanism is expected to provide a flexible and generalizable approach to variance control for post-training quantization, with improved accuracy and robustness compared to existing methods. However, its performance may degrade in scenarios with highly non-linear or complex models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comprehensive Comparison of Post-Training Quantization Methods for VGGT
PROPOSAL: Provide a comprehensive comparison of the different post-training quantization methods proposed in this research agenda (e.g., linear quantization, constrained minimization, EMAs, model-agnostic variance control) on a wide range of VGGT setups and datasets, including multi-view 3D reconstruction, camera pose estimation, point map, and point cloud reconstruction.
CONTROLS: Compare the performance of each quantization method against a baseline of full-precision VGGT, and against each other. Investigate the robustness of each method to different calibration datasets and sampling methods.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This comprehensive comparison will provide insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each post-training quantization method, and will enable the selection of the most suitable method for a given application and scenario. However, the sheer scale of the experiment may lead to challenges in terms of computational resources and dataset management.

TITLE: Investigating the Effects of Special Tokens on Quantization Error in VGGT
PROPOSAL: Analyze the sensitivity of VGGT's accuracy to the quantization error of special tokens, camera tokens, register tokens, and learned frame embeddings separately, using PTQ with fixed precision and varying calibration sets. This will identify the most critical component affecting quantization results and help develop targeted solutions.
CONTROLS: Compare against full-precision model performance and against PTQ of the whole VGGT model without separate token analysis.
COST: 10 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the camera token and learned frame embeddings to have the largest impact on quantization error, as the non-image tokens are injected fixed and independent from the image tokens. However, the effect of special tokens variety may lead to unexpected results where certain token comparison is more sensitive than others, where if PTQ can effectively handle a combination of structure tokens can this would open the path for general VGGT based architecture design that can benefit from more knowledge & efficiency.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE:  Adaptive Quantization Strategy for Data-Independent Tokens in VGGT
PROPOSAL: Develop a learning-based approach to adaptively adjust the quantization bins for data-independent special tokens, camera tokens, and register tokens. Use a small auxiliary network to predict the optimal quantization bins based on the token's input and output distributions. This adaptive strategy should enable more effective handling of the heavy-tailed distributions characteristic of special tokens.
CONTROLS: Compare against the fixed-bin quantization approach in proposal 1, and investigate the efficacy of different architectures for the auxiliary network (e.g., tiny MLPs, sparse reference networks).
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the adaptive quantization strategy to improve VGGT's accuracy under PTQ, with a potential trade-off in increased inference time due to the auxiliary network. The performance gain will largely depend on the complexity and quality of the auxiliary network. If its effect on performance isn't large enough in efficiency-cost trade-off then ablation studies may help to navigate those effects.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Exploiting Structural Knowledge in VGGT for More Efficient Calibration
PROPOSAL: Utilize the structural knowledge about the camera poses, scene geometry, and the point map representations in VGGT to generate representative calibration samples. This can be achieved by creatively sampling viewpoints, poses, and point map configurations that are likely to capture the major parts of the data distribution.
CONTROLS: Compare against random sampling calibration and ablate the effect of different selection strategies on quantization performance.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect this approach to substantially improve the robustness and generalizability of the VGGT PTQ, as it leverages prior knowledge of the 3D reconstruction task to sample a more representative set of calibration samples.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE:  Structured Calibration for Efficient PTQ in VGGT
PROPOSAL: Refine proposal 3's structured knowledge approach to generate more calibrated and diverse calibration samples by incorporating an iterative process that optimizes the sampling strategy with respect to the target tasks (pixel-wise depth, camera pose, and point map regression). This can be achieved by iteratively refining the sampling strategy through a customized objective (e.g., maximizing calibration coverage, or minimizing the gap between model performance on the calibration set and unseen samples).
CONTROLS: Compare against single-step structural sampling and random sampling calibration, and investigate the effect of different iteration strategies and objectives on quantization performance.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: By incorporating an iterative refinement step, this structured calibration approach is expected to yield even better results than proposal 3, with a potential reduction in calibration error and better generalization to unseen samples. However, this increase in computational cost may offset some of the benefits of PTQ, and ablation studies are required to identify the optimal trade-off.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Quantization-Aware Label Smoothing for Improved Calibration
PROPOSAL: Introduce an additional regularization term in the quantization calibration process by incorporating label smoothing on the target tasks (pixel-wise depth, camera pose, and point map regression). This is intended to improve the stability and generalizability of the quantized model by adding a pseudo-output distribution centered around the ground truth, thereby reducing overfitting and improving the robustness of the quantization calibration process.
CONTROLS: Compare against the standard quantization calibration process without label smoothing, and investigate the effect of different amounts of label smoothing on calibration performance.
COST: 20 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect label smoothing to improve the calibration performance of the quantized model by reducing overfitting and stabilizing the calibration process. The optimal amount of label smoothing will need to be determined through hyperparameter tuning and validation.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Domain Adaptation for PTQ: Exploring Transfer Learning to Overcome Calibration Shift
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of domain adaptation techniques to overcome calibration shift caused by the PTQ process. Specifically, fine-tune a pre-trained VGGT model on a new domain (e.g., a different indoor or outdoor dataset, with varying lighting conditions, scene complexities, etc.) to adapt to the quantized representation space.
CONTROLS: Compare against training from scratch or using a full-precision pre-trained model for PTQ, and investigate the effect of different domain adaptation strategies and pre-training tasks on calibration performance.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect domain adaptation to improve the calibration performance of the PTQ model by adapting to the new domain and overcoming the calibration shift. However, this comes at the cost of increased computational resources and potential overfitting issues. The effectiveness of domain adaptation will depend on the discrepancy between the pre-training and target domains.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-Temperature Discriminative Calibration for Improved Quantization Performance
PROPOSAL: Employ a multi-temperature discriminative calibration approach to refine the quantization calibration process by iteratively refining the quantization decision boundaries based on a probabilistic temperature schedule. This can be achieved by formulating the calibration problem as a multi-temperature discriminative calibration task, where the temperature schedule controls the balance between calibration error and model performance.
CONTROLS: Compare against single-temperature discriminative calibration, and investigate the effect of different temperature schedules and calibration objectives on calibration performance.
COST: 60 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the multi-temperature discriminative calibration approach to improve the calibration performance by iteratively refining the quantization decision boundaries, leading to better adaptation to the target data distribution. However, this comes at the cost of increased computational time and potential overfitting issues if the temperature schedule is not carefully chosen.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Hypernetwork-based Quantization Mask Learning for Efficient PTQ
PROPOSAL: Utilize a hypernetwork architecture to learn a quantization mask that optimizes the quantization process by selecting which features or channels to quantize and which to maintain in full precision. This approach combines the benefits of sparse attention and efficient quantization, allowing for a more flexible and adaptive quantization strategy.
CONTROLS: Compare against fixed-precision quantization, uniform quantization, and adaptive quantization approaches, and investigate the effect of different hypernetwork architectures and regularization techniques on quantization performance.
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the hypernetwork-based quantization mask learning approach to significantly improve the efficiency of PTQ by strategically selecting which channels to quantize and which to maintain in full precision, leading to better trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost. However, the design of the hypernetwork and the quantization mask selection process will require careful tuning and optimization to achieve the best results.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unified Framework for PTQ: Customizable Task-Agnostic Calibration
PROPOSAL: Develop a unified framework that integrates the proposed methods (special token quantization, adaptive quantization strategy, structured calibration, quantization-aware label smoothing, domain adaptation, multi-temperature discriminative calibration, and hypernetwork-based quantization mask learning) to provide a customizable and task-agnostic calibration approach for PTQ. This framework will enable the selection of the most effective combination of techniques and hyperparameters for a given PTQ task, optimizing the trade-off between calibration error, model performance, and computational cost.
CONTROLS: Evaluate the framework on a comprehensive set of PTQ tasks, including image segmentation, object detection, and 3D reconstruction, and compare against state-of-the-art PTQ methods.
COST: 400 GPU-hours ( Note: Cumulative compute cost of the previous proposals will be deducted from this estimate)
PREDICTION: We expect the unified framework to provide a robust and versatile PTQ solution, enabling significant improvements in calibration accuracy and model efficiency across a wide range of tasks and applications. However, the optimization of the framework's hyperparameters and the selection of the most effective combination of techniques will require thorough validation and tuning.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating the Effects of Special Token Quantization in VGGT
PROPOSAL: This experiment will focus on the effect of quantizing the data-independent special tokens (camera and register tokens) in the VGGT model to understand their role in overall performance and accuracy of camera pose estimation, point map and point cloud reconstruction. We will use the ScanNet dataset, which is a common benchmark in multi-view 3D reconstruction, and compare the full-precision model against various special token quantization schemes (e.g. fixed-point, learned rounding, and uniform quantization).
CONTROLS: Full-precision VGGT model, pointcloud/voxel-based reconstruction methods (e.g. MinkowskiNet), previous quantization schemes applied for 2D vision transformers
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: The results will show that the special token quantization significantly affects the overall performance of VGGT, with the precise effect depending on the quantization scheme used. We expect that learned rounding would generally perform better than uniform quantization.

Facilitating this study is the fact that  experiments have shown significant improvement when these special tokens were turned ON in previous VGGT architectures for better performance.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigating Calibration Set Generation for VGGT Quantization
PROPOSAL: To handle the heavy-tailed activation statistics and ensure representative calibration samples, we will investigate different calibration set generation methods for VGGT, such as dividing the dataset into clusters based on view angles, and selecting the most diverse samples from each cluster. Alternatively, we will consider using an autoencoder-based approach to select diverse calibration samples from the entire dataset. We will evaluate these methods using the GATet dataset, a challenging real-world multi-view 3D reconstruction benchmark.
CONTROLS: Clustering methods (e.g. K-means, Hierarchical clustering), random sampling, target-decayed entropy-based sampling
COST: 200 GPU-hours
 PREDICTION: Our results will demonstrate the importance of choosing the right calibration set, showing that diversifying the samples significantly improves the robustness and generalization of the obtained quantization ranges. Clustering based methods are likely to demonstrate the better robustness.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Comparative Study of Quantization Techniques for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We will examine various post-training quantization techniques (e.g. dynamic fixed-point, Huffman coding, and entropy coding) and evaluate their impact on the accuracy of camera pose estimation and 3D reconstruction tasks in VGGT. We will compare the performance of these techniques with existing state-of-the-art quantization methods applied to 2D vision transformers. Our experiments will be conducted on the NYU-Depth-V2 and Matterport3D datasets, which consist of diverse indoor scenes and viewpoints.
CONTROLS: Quantization-aware training, k-means clustering and uniform quantization, bit-wise scaling methods
COST: 250 GPU-hours
 PREDICTION: Our comparative study will show that quantization techniques specifically designed for VGGT outperform existing techniques, offering competitive performance in terms of camera pose estimation and 3D reconstruction tasks.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: Comparative Study of Quantization Techniques for VGGT
PROPOSAL: We will investigate further how different data distributions affect the performance of the various quantization techniques in VGGT by also specifically examining the impact of quantization on the learned camera and register tokens. Using the same dataset ensemble from our revised proposal, we will apply a perturbation analysis to evaluate how model changes (due to quantization) in the network's camera and register tokens propagate through the model and result in corresponding changes in estimated camera poses and 3D reconstructions.
CONTROLS: The standard NYU-Depth-V2 and Matterport3D datasets will be used to validate these perturbation-based results across the ensemble of datasets where data complexity varies.
COST: 50 additional GPU-hours, not affecting the total under 300 GPU-hours  
 PREDICTION: We hope that this deeper analysis identifies which quantization methods tend to significantly alter the camera and register tokens in ways most in line with actual visual geometry transformations, providing deeper, model-specific insights.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Theoretical Analysis of Quantization Error Propagation in VGGT
PROPOSAL: This theoretical work will provide an understanding of how quantization affects the geometry output of VGGT by analyzing the propagation of quantization errors through the model's architecture. We will examine the loss of information due to quantization during feature transformations and aggregation in the transformer backbone and point transformer module. This analysis will also inform a set of proposals for using the layer-wise information to estimate more effective, model-conditional quantization steps for activation and weight. 
CONTROLS: The formulations will be evaluated on both the NYU-Depth-V2 and Matterport3D datasets.
COST: 75 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: We anticipate that our theoretical analysis will reveal a technique to bound and/or model the total amount of information lost due to quantization, providing a principled approach for setting the resolution of activation quantization based on a curated description of task relevance (such as keeping latent information accurate by doing a NEC bound - Noise in the Exact Corrections).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Model-Conditional Quantization Techniques for VGGT
PROPOSAL: Building on the theoretical analysis of quantization error propagation, we will design and evaluate a range of model-conditional quantization techniques tailored to VGGT's architecture. These include quantizing the feature maps based on their task relevance, using knowledge distillation to fine-tune the quantization parameters, and employing learning-based approaches to dynamically adjust the quantization scales at each layer. We will also examine the applicability of existing model-conditional quantization methods developed for 2D vision transformers. 
CONTROLS:  State-of-the-art models for 2D vision and some sample applications, standard VGGT with learned token quantization 
COST: 120 GPU-hours 
PREDICTION: Our work should lead to quantized VGGT models with significant memory savings and speed-ups, demonstrating the ability to maintain, and preferably slightly surpass the accuracy of the full-precision variants.

We will investigate hierarchical quantization approaches, where the precision is adaptively varied across different layers and even individual attention heads, along with fine-grained parallel and serial quantization techniques tailored to the specifics of the VGGT architecture.

ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Quantization Baseline with VGGT
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the full-precision VGGT model on a standard multi-view 3D reconstruction benchmark, such as the DTU-Multi-View dataset, to establish a baseline for camera pose estimation and point map/point cloud reconstruction performance.
CONTROLS: Train the full-precision VGGT model from scratch on a large-scale dataset (e.g., NYU Depth V2 or MatterPort3D), and fine-tune it on the DTU-Multi-View dataset.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours (full-precision model training on 16 V100 GPUs for 10 hours).
PREDICTION: Expect the baseline performance to set a high bar, rivaling or surpassing state-of-the-art (SOTA) results. Fail when the quantization of VGGT incurs severe performance degradation due to the high-dimensional and highly redundant semantic space of 3D data.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Sample Diversity Metrics for Calibration Set Selection
PROPOSAL: Introduce and analyze various metrics to assess the diversity of the calibration set used for post-training quantization of VGGT. Investigate the impact of calibration set size, component diversity, and dissimilarity on quantization performance, by considering metrics such as entropy, mutual information, and statistical distance between the calibration set and the full dataset.
CONTROLS: Split the calibration set into various subsets with different diversity levels (e.g., images from different scenes, poses, lighting conditions, and occlusions) and evaluate their performance.
COST: 50 GPU-hours (simulations, metric computations, and performance evaluation).
PREDICTION: Expect these metrics to help identify the most diverse and representative calibration sets. However, fail when the complexity of 3D data and the presence of outliers hinder the effectiveness of these metrics, requiring a more comprehensive approach to quantization.

ACTION: ADD 3
